recipes.name: Easy Punch
ingredients_raw: 4 (0.13 ounce) packages unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder

steps.text: Combine water, pineapple juice, sugar, and drink mix powder in a large punch bowl; stir until sugar and drink mix powder dissolve. Stir in ginger ale.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Punch
raw_recipe.description: This easy punch recipe blends strawberry drink mix, pineapple juice, sugar, water, and ginger ale together for a bright, fruity, refreshing beverage.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Punch
recipeIngredient: 4 (0.13 ounce) packages unsweetened strawberry-flavored drink mix powder

recipeInstructions.text: Combine water, pineapple juice, sugar, and drink mix powder in a large punch bowl; stir until sugar and drink mix powder dissolve. Stir in ginger ale.

review.reviewBody: I made this punch recipe for a baby shower. Everyone loved it! I mixed everything but the ginger ale together and froze it a few days before the shower. The day of the shower, I took the punch from the freezer about an hour before serving to let it thaw a little. Put it in my punch bowl and added the ginger ale. It made a delicious slushy punch. I will definately use this recipe again in the future. Thanks for sharing!!
I made this punch for a get together and everyone loved it. The only change I made was to use only half cup sugar which was plenty. Great recipe and very easy. Will definitely make again!

So easy and loved by my coworkers and boss; in fact, it's the punch recipe my boss REQUESTS. (Unfortunately, that means the punch is always my responsibility!..)

For smaller functions it's easy to halve the recipe, but no matter what, DEFINITELY cut back on the sugar. Even using 1/8th of what's called for can be on the sweet side.

As another reviewer mentioned, if you freeze the mixture (everything but the ginger ale), the punch gets a slight slushy texture and stays cold longer without adding ice. (But, perhaps additional ice cuts back on the sweetness?)

In my area strawberry drink powder (aka Kool-Aid) is hard to find, so I use a tropical fruit mix instead.

My family really enjoyed this punch. I did change some things to make it more diabetic friendly and I also halved it. I used 2 packets of sugar free strawberry drink mix, 1 liter diet ginger ale, 1 qt water and 1 can pineapple juice to make 1 gallon. Very good, even with it being sugar free, it didn't taste like a diet drink.

Love this recipe! I'm in the Red Hat Society, as the Queen of the Chapter, I made this our "signature" punch ... except it's so easy, it's embarrassing to "give out the recipe", they all thought it was this complicated recipe. I don't freeze like other suggested, I keep chilled and assemble before Red Hat sisters arrive adding crushed ice. Been making for last 3 yrs at home events. Overtime, I have reduced sugar to 2c - 2-1/2c to help the ladies watching their sugar, and I use diet ginger ale.

Easy and soooo delicious! I followed the advice of others and prepared everything but the ginger ale the night before and froze it. I took it out of the freezer and transferred it to the punch bowl three hours ahead of time, and added the ginger ale at the end. It made a great slushy punch everyone loved. The next time I tried it, I was looking for something more adult and added some coconut rum with the ginger ale. YOWZA! It was almost a little too good! ;)

This was such an easy recipe to follow and use. I upped the quantities to serve over 300 kids at their 8th grade dance, and they loved it. I made the punch up ahead of time, minus the ginger ale. Then, I poured equal portions of punch and ginger ale in the punch dispenser when we were ready to serve it. We also had water available for the kids, which they drank too. 
These teenagers loved this punch so much that they drained my almost 10 gallons of punch - draining my punch bowl dry each time. 
What a hit! 
Note - we ended up using Fruit Punch Koolade, because we couldn't find any strawberry. Still was a success!!!

I made this recipe for a baby shower and it got good reviews. I used fruit punch rather than strawberry, cut the recipe in half, and used diet ginger-ale to cut some of the sweetness. I ended up using double the amount of ginger ale for half the recipe. This recipe is versatile because you can experiment with different flavors. I will probably make again.

I made this for a small New Year’s Eve party and it was a huge hit. I didn’t need quite the full recipe, so I used 3 pkgs strawberry Kool-Aid, (1) 46 oz can pineapple juice, a little over 2 liters of diet ginger ale, and approx 1 3/4 cup sugar. Added just a little water, didn’t measure it. It was refreshing and delicious.

I halved this recipe and it was perfect for my baby shower of 18. Like other reviewers said, mix everything but the ginger ale the night before and freeze it, then take it out about 5-7 hours before the event to thaw then add the ginger ale to serve.

Made this for a friend's wedding, about 100 people. It was easy, inexpensive and delicious. I had to transport it, so followed Phyllis' suggestion to freeze most of it ahead of time. I divided and put the punch mixture into Ziploc freezer bags and froze. Then, when it was time to serve, I left the bags out to defrost for a bit, dumped the semi-defrosted mixture in the punch bowl and poured the ginger ale over. Slushy yumminess! A huge hit with the happy couple and guests.
Easy, good and measurements are perfect

It was super easy to make, but no one drank it more than 1x! It was a 90° hot day. I used Cherry koolaide flavor packets. It was bitter tasting using the ginger ale . Also tried it with sprite and it wasn't any better.

This is one of My Grandmother"s punch recipes she use to make . And my Favorite! The only difference was she would Half the batch to freeze a ring of the punch then add it. And then the Ginger ale right before serving.

I don't much care for fruit punch, but made this for a beverage at a Taco Bar buffet. It was delicious. Believe it or not, I made it exactly following the recipe!. Everyone who tried it liked it. This makes a LOT of punch. I will make this again.
Super delicious! Didn't change anything. Everyone loved it for our girl's night out - they couldn't get enough! Not a drop left! Definitely a keeper for next time.
Great base! Definitely benefits from the juice of a couple fresh lemons and a bit more carbonation.
added juice from mandarin oranges and seltzer water. very good. my brother is asking for more.
I've made this a few times. It's always a hit during the holiday season. As a few others noted, I recommend cutting back on the sugar some unless you want it to be super sweet.

I was not very impressed by this punch. I followed exactly (other than using less sugar as other reviewers suggested) and I still thought it was very sweet. Believe me, I've got a sweet tooth! Made it for a party with all ages in attendance, and it was the least used drink available. Don't think I'll be making this one again.
